acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Boars family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Tunnel Boar, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Brace-and-Charge Soldier archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Thick-necked cave boar with worn forehead, longer tusks, mud-packed coat, and reinforced shoulder callus.
Signature mechanic: Tunnel Brace: both hind legs lock before a long charge that gains power in narrow terrain but cannot evade obstacles.
battlefieldDuty: Brace inside narrow ground and drive targets out of cover with a long committed charge.
constructionDimensions: Packed soil and mineral plates reinforce the forehead, shoulders, hooves, and tusk bases while hide and bristles remain dominant.
Charges peel up coherent furrows and detached stones that follow the exact route.
counterplay: Leave the lane or make the Boar collide with solid terrain, exposing its stunned forehead and flank. Affinity signal: A pale fracture seam opens at the planted hoof or outside shoulder when the Boar commits to turning or bracing.
forbiddenTreatments: Random floating rocks unrelated to the charge route
identityInvariants: Every form keeps a low four-legged boar body, cloven hooves, mobile snout, raised bristles, short tail, and visible tusk roots.
Tier escalation uses tusk geometry, neck mass, shoulder callus, scars, and bristle profile rather than humanoid equipment.
Charge direction remains readable through hoof placement, lowered head angle, tusk contact, dust, and the alignment of the spine.
telegraph: Both hind hooves settle and dust funnels backward along the future lane.
